item.title: [github_trending] morluto/rea
item.description: REA is an open-source MCP tool from morluto that lets agents reverse engineer across application runtime behavior and native binaries, so a feature you like can be traced down to its binary-level implementation. It ships as the npm package rea-agents, requires Node.js 22.19+, and is MIT licensed. It targets security researchers and anyone who wants an agent doing binary analysis.

item.title: [juejin] Cursor 转 Codex 大半个月，聊聊我的真实感受
item.description: A Juejin post in which a developer describes spending roughly half a month in Codex after switching from Cursor. His takeaway is that Cursor still reads as an AI coding assistant, while Codex feels closer to a general-purpose agent that carries out tasks on its own. Useful for developers deciding which tool to adopt for daily work.

item.description: A Juejin article argues the 2026 technical interview has changed: where two years ago candidates were asked to hand-write a Promise or explain React Fiber, interviewers now assume you work with AI and ask something else — if AI can write 80% of the code, why does the company still need you? item.title: [v2ex] [硬件] 光模块里那颗 DSP 占了近一半功耗， LPO 和 CPO 都想把它拿掉
item.description: A V2EX post walks through the power budget of AI data-center optics: a SemiAnalysis teardown puts the DSP inside an 800G module at nearly half its power draw, and an 18,000-GPU cluster needs roughly 46,000 modules. Two DSP-free routes are compared — LPO trims 30–50%, while CPO cuts a single 800G port from 16–17W to 4–5W. Broadcom shipped CPO switches to customers in 2024, with Nvidia's Ethernet CPO set for H2 2026. Useful for operators weighing power savings against field-replaceability.

item.description: The maintainer of chinese-independent-blogs, a GitHub repo listing Chinese independent blogs that has reached 24k stars, launched indi.blog — it subscribes to every listed blog that has an RSS feed and lets readers like and comment. The homepage ranks posts with a Hacker News-style algorithm, and with dozens of new entries a day it works as a browsable feed for occasional reading.

item.description: This Java roundup covers Atmosphere 4.0 reaching GA, GraalVM 25.3 with a new SubstratePriorityInliningPhase inliner for JIT and Native Image plus security hardening, a WildFly 41 maintenance release, and milestone builds of Jakarta Data 1.1.0 and Eclipse JNoSQL. On the JDK side, JEP 542 (PEM Encodings of Cryptographic Objects) is now Targeted for JDK 28 after three preview rounds in JDK 25 through 27. It's a quick way for Java developers to catch up on ecosystem releases.

item.title: [github_trending] DuarteSantos8/openGym
item.description: openGym is a self-hosted gym and body-weight tracker: plan your week, run guided workouts, log every set including supersets, warm-ups and cardio, and see which muscles are trained, fatigued or detrained. It imports data from FitNotes, Strong and Hevy, and uses passkey login with sync across your own devices. Best for lifters who want to own their training data rather than rent it from a subscription app.

item.title: [juejin] 三年了，为什么 AI 应用还没爆发？
item.description: A Juejin article starts from Meta's "compute glut" story and the resulting plunge in AI stocks to ask why AI applications still haven't taken off, when an AI-native Douyin, WeChat or Xiaohongshu will appear, and whether this cycle repeats the 2000 dot-com bust. It's written for developers and practitioners watching AI adoption timelines and industry cycles.

item.title: [hackernews] Claude Haiku 5.5
item.description: Claude Haiku 5.5 is positioned as the fastest and most capable small model yet, aimed at high-volume work such as summarization, subagents and browser use. The release note gives no benchmarks or pricing, so the claim rests on the vendor's own description. Teams running high-throughput pipelines should treat it as a candidate to test.

item.title: [juejin] 被吹上天的 JWT，为什么主流网站一个都不用
item.description: Using github.com as the example, the author notes its cookies contain just a single _gh_session value — Rails-encrypted session data — to explain why mainstream sites keep state on the server rather than packing it into a JWT. It is aimed at backend developers choosing an authentication strategy and wondering where JWTs actually fall short in production.

item.title: [github_trending] mattpocock/skills
item.description: mattpocock/skills is a collection of agent skills pulled straight from the author's own .agents directory, aimed at doing real engineering rather than vibe coding. They are deliberately small, composable and easy to adapt, and work with any model. The author positions them against approaches like GSD, BMAD and Spec-Kit, which own the process and make process bugs hard to fix.

item.title: [github_trending] tester-army/e2e
item.description: TesterArmy's e2e is an open-source, AI-driven end-to-end testing framework for web and mobile apps, published on npm as the `e2e` package under Apache-2.0. Teams that maintain large UI test suites and want to cut down on selector and script maintenance may want to evaluate it.

He filed a DMCA notice on September 4, and a month later GitHub replied that it could not confirm a violation of 17 U.S. Code § 1201; he is now asking whether to hire a lawyer.
